items.content_html:
Bureau will still dismiss those engaged with sex workers within past 10 years, three or more times overall, or while in public safety capacity

The FBI is dropping a categorical hiring ban on applicants who have had sexual encounters with sex workers and will instead consider in a more holistic manner at least some candidates who have engaged in the practice in the past, according to people familiar with the matter.

The move away from an automatic disqualification falls along a continuum of evolving recruitment standards within federal law enforcement and at the buttoned-up bureau, which several years ago relaxed its approach to candidates’ past marijuana use and has drawn more recent concern among some current and former agents about a perceived loosening of recruitment requirements as it seeks to replenish its ranks.

A schoolgirl smiling in her uniform; a beaming, chubby-cheeked baby; a couple smiling on their wedding day; a young man, hands on hips, atop a mountain peak; a young girl with flowing hair, peaking out from behind a door.

These faces are just a fraction of the thousands who have not been seen since deadly flash floods coursed through the Himalayas and wiped away entire villages. By Saturday morning, the toll of the missing had risen to almost 3,000, in both Nepal and Tibet.

items.title: La tragédie au Népal met en garde contre un danger croissant : 15 millions de personnes vivent sous la menace des lacs glaciaires
items.content_html:
La inondation monstrueuse du Tibet et du Népal, qui a causé des centaines de morts et des milliers de personnes disparues, a rendu le risque de vivre en montagne des chaînes de montagnes avec des glaciers, puisque tout indique qu'une de ces masses de glace s'est effondrée et a déclenché la tragédie. Le phénomène est connu sous le nom de GLOF (Glacier Lake Outburst Flood), une crue soudaine provoquée par le débordement d'un lac glaciaire. Le le changement climatique et son augmentation des températures sont à l'origine de ces événements : les inondations ont été multipliées par six au siècle dernier. Les grandes chaînes de montagnes comme l'Himalaya, les Andes ou les Alpes concentrent les endroits où se produisent le plus ce type d'inondations, auxquelles sont exposées 15 millions de personnes dans le monde, dont la moitié au Pérou, en Inde, en Chine et au Pakistan. Surveiller les glaciers et les lagons n'est pas facile, surtout dans les pays en développement, mais cela sauve des vies : l'année dernière, une ville de Suisse a été évacuée deux jours avant l'effondrement d'un autre glacier.

items.content_html: The wildfires this summer have broken records in Germany and are unlikely to subside in future. Psychologists say post-traumatic stress disorder caused by such disasters is serious but can be treated if people seek help.

items.content_html: Bernadette Amani is heading into her first full season with Bayern Munich, having joined the club in January. Making a living at football is something she never imagined possible while growing up in rural Ivory Coast.

items.content_html: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, but none owns a fixed share. A 2018 convention established rules for navigation, security and fishing while leaving some seabed borders unresolved.

items.title: Messi retirement hint highlights football era nearing an end
items.content_html: Soon after propelling Argentina to a second consecutive World Cup final, Lionel Messi has cast some doubt on his future. While retirement doesn't seem imminent, it still beckons for him and Cristiano Ronaldo.

items.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
items.content_html: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

items.title: Will Germany's drought push up food prices?
items.content_html: Germany's main farmers' association has warned of a below-average harvest after drought and crops damaged by extreme heat. DW looks into what lower yields could mean for food prices and grocery bills.

items.title: Dressed for power: Giorgia Meloni and the language of fashion
items.content_html: From Giorgia Meloni's shift from dark suits to pastels to Angela Merkel's signature jackets, politicians have long used clothing to shape how voters see them. In this day and age, power dressing has evolved.

items.title: How to grow food for more people in a hotter world
items.content_html: Inside futuristic labs, plants are scanned, stressed and analyzed. The aim is to use the results to produce plant strains that can better serve a growing population in a warming world.

items.content_html: Created in Germany and now a global success, Hyrox combines running and functional training into a unique format. How a German concept became an international sports phenomenon.

items.title: Do not inhale! How wildfire smoke 'affects the whole body'
items.content_html: Wildfires destroy lives and livelihoods. But survivors and firefighters also suffer long-term harm to their health. A growing body of research suggests particulate matter (PM2.5) in wildfire smoke is a major culprit.

items.title: Germany: Bundeswehr troop numbers reach 13-year high
items.content_html: Germany's Defense Ministry is reporting a comparatively rare success story in its bid to bolster troop numbers. At the end of July, the total stood at around 186,700, roughly 3,700 more than a year earlier — a 2% boost.
